<description>
This doesn't fix the general case of rebroadcasting potentially surprising users by divulging the originator IP trivially, but for users opting into private broadcast, it seems a bridge too far for them to expect the current behavior.

e.g. an incoming dust payment triggering your node to rebroadcast 24-36th later over clearnet

This can be removed if/when wallet drives through private broadcast.

see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/3828 for running broader issue
</description>

<new_statements>
[2026-09-29] c:5883120907 comment by andrewtoth (member):
[quoted text omitted]

I was merely suggesting to have the wallet rebroadcast via private broadcast if `-privatebroadcast` was set, not fix the entire unexpected rebroadcasting issue by requiring `-privatebroadcast`. (Although I might have shared that idea in another channel, I am not advocating we do that here.)
[2026-09-29] c:5887071448 comment by vasild (member):
Improving privacy is good, but I think this has taken an odd approach:

* It adds a relationship between wallet behavior and `-privatebroadcast`. It is documented that `-privatebroadcast` does not affect the wallet.

* It makes it impossible to have `-privatebroadcast=1` and wallet rebroadcast. Wallet rebroadcast indeed looks bad wrt privacy, but it is so even without considering `-privatebroadcast`. There may be setups where the wallet rebroadcasts are not so bad (e.g. if the node is not directly connected to clearnet) and are desired. Wallet rebroadcasts shouldn't really be tied to the value of `-privatebroadcast`.

I think it is better to make wallet rebroadcasts separately controllable, independently of `-privatebroadcast`. Opened https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36380 to explore that.
</new_statements>
